title: Newtypes and Extension Traits
goal: Wrap types for safety and add methods to external types.

sections.text: You know primitive types like integer and string in Java or Go. In Rust, wrapping a primitive in a tuple struct creates a completely distinct type.

sections.caption: UserId and OrderId cannot be swapped by accident.

sections.text: The compiler rejects passing a raw `u32` or an `OrderId` to `process`. This pattern costs nothing at runtime because the wrapper disappears during compilation.
You may also want to add methods to existing standard types like `str`. Writing an `impl` directly on a foreign type fails with error `E0116`.

sections.caption: Define a trait in your crate to extend standard types.

sections.text: This rule is called the orphan rule. To add a method to a foreign type, define a local trait in your crate and implement that trait for the type.

explanation: Wrap types for safety and add methods to external types.
